learnings.question: What three core roles are described as giving human life its ultimate purpose in Islamic teaching?
options: Seeking wealth, status, and physical pleasure
Worshiping Allah, serving as a steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and living a life of accountability in preparation for the Hereafter
Praying five times a day, fasting, and giving charity
Following cultural traditions, respecting elders, and preserving family honor
learnings.learning: Human purpose in Islam is framed around three roles: worshiping Allah, acting as a steward (khalifah) over the Earth, and living a life of free will and accountability in preparation for the Hereafter.

learnings.question: What term describes the heightened mindfulness of God's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies a person's intentions?
learnings.learning: Taqwa is the mindfulness of Allah's presence cultivated through worship; it builds self-restraint, purifies intentions, and guides a person away from wrongdoing.

learnings.question: In a teaching about divine justice, what happens to even the smallest possible deed, described as being as small as an atom's weight?
options: It is averaged together with a person's other deeds
It is forgiven automatically regardless of good or evil
It is fully accounted for, whether it was good or evil
It is ignored since only major deeds are judged
learnings.learning: Divine justice accounts for every deed no matter how small — even an act as small as an atom's weight of good or evil will be seen — reinforcing that no righteous effort is wasted.

learnings.question: Roughly how many distinct words exist in the Arabic language, compared to around 170,000 in the Oxford English Dictionary?
options: About 170,000, roughly the same as English
learnings.learning: Arabic has an estimated 12 million distinct words compared to roughly 170,000 in English — an approximate 71:1 ratio — one reason the analysis used the original Arabic text of the Quran rather than an English translation.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: When the Pareto Principle (the 80/20 rule) was tested against actual word-frequency data from the Quran, what share of the text did the 20 most frequently used words turn out to make up?
learnings.learning: A data analysis of word frequency in the Quran found the 20 most common words account for only about 20.83% of the text, disproving the assumption that the Pareto Principle's 80/20 split would hold.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what is the term for the actual, lived unfolding of events in a person's life — shaped by their own actions and decisions, and able to be influenced through sincere supplication?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, which can be influenced by sincere Dua and action, while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal knowledge and plan that already encompasses any such change.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: What central lesson is drawn from the teaching that a people's circumstances will not change until they change what is within themselves?
options: A person has a responsibility to take action and make genuine internal change in order for their circumstances to improve
A person's circumstances are fixed and cannot be changed by any action
Only verbal prayer, without any accompanying action, can change one's fate
A person's circumstances change at random and are unrelated to their own choices
learnings.learning: A key teaching on fate holds that a person is responsible for their own circumstances and must take genuine action and seek inner change — doing so alters their Qada', even though that change was always encompassed within Allah's Qadr.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In Surah Al-Mu'minoon, what term is used for the idle, meaningless speech — drama, gossip, and pointless chatter — that successful believers are urged to turn away from?
learnings.learning: The Quran uses the term 'Lagw' for ill or meaningless speech — drama, gossip, idle chatter — and describes turning away from it as a mark of a successful believer.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which economist and political scientist is credited with the 1971 observation that an information-rich world necessarily creates a scarcity of attention?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that in an information-rich world, the wealth of information creates a corresponding scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of whoever receives it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In the Scrum agile framework, which artifact visualizes a sprint's progress by showing the work still remaining, helping a team track whether it's on schedule?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is one of Scrum's three core artifacts; it visualizes a sprint's progress and shows remaining work so the team can track whether they're on schedule.

learnings.question: In Scrum, which of the three key roles is specifically responsible for defining a product's needed features and prioritizing the product backlog?
learnings.learning: The Product Owner is one of Scrum's three key roles, responsible for defining the features a product needs and prioritizing the product backlog, distinct from the Scrum Master and the Developers.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist is credited with demonstrating that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it — the basis for spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What is the name for the psychological phenomenon in which simply writing information down, or saving it digitally, causes the brain to treat that information as safe to forget?
options: The Performance Paradox of Cognitive Offloading (also called Digital Amnesia)
learnings.learning: Psychologists call it the 'Performance Paradox' of Cognitive Offloading, also known as Digital Amnesia: the moment information is written down or saved digitally, the brain treats that as permission to forget it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents the device as almost completely powered down, used for the longest periods of inactivity, and resulting in both the highest power savings and the longest wake-up time?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power management state, leaving the device almost completely powered down; it delivers the highest power savings but takes the longest time to wake up and resume activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state is the lightest sleep mode — meant only for very brief idle periods — allowing the link to wake almost instantly and resume full activity?
learnings.learning: L0s is PCIe's lightest low-power state, designed for very short idle periods; the link can quickly wake from it to resume full activity, unlike the deeper and slower-waking L1 and L2 states.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe
